https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/47300 is the same change right ?

Thanks for the question.
These are different changes. 47300 is for the Chassis collection, while my change (87018) focuses on the Systems/Processors collection. Although they both retrieve data from the xyz.openbmc_project.Control.Power.Cap interface on D-Bus, they represent power limits at different hardware levels.
Acknowledged

With this change we are going to be looking across much more of the D-Bus tree whenever we are looking for processors. Is this really desirable or correct? (I.e. Since this method is used for handleProcessorGet also.)
Done

Should be using object_path methods for comparison.

See: https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/docs/COMMON_ERRORS.md#12-imprecise-matching
Done

Looks like this loop was added due to the increase in the search of the getSubTree() call in order to support finding the Power.Cap object.

Why not use an association to get from the Processor to the object implementing the Power.Cap interface? I see a in-progress commit in phosphor-dbus-interfaces to define the association: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/86744

Thank you for the suggestion. Using associations is much more efficient than performing a broad getSubTree search.

I will modify the code to origin way and then follow the association defined in 86744 to retrieve the related Power.Cap object.
Done
Should be able to use std::ranges here
Done

Guidelines for this repo is to not used lambdas longer than 10 lines. Please refactor this into a named function.

See: https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/docs/COMMON_ERRORS.md#14-very-long-lambda-callbacks
Done
Use sdbusplus::unpackPropertiesNoThrow() instead for unpacking the properties.
Done

I don't see the definition of this value (std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max()) as undefined in the phosphor-dbus-interfaces. Is this specific to a distribution?

I think the PDI should be updated to document the meaning of this value with community acceptance in order to add this special-case handling in bmcweb.

https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/bb79ddd0c8173b9a90ddcc578808e5c03e63ae30/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Control/Power/Cap.interface.yaml#L5

You are right. We have proposed an update to the PowerCap description in PDI to formally document that std::numeric_limits<uint32_t>::max() (0xFFFFFFFF) represents an undefined or uninitialized state: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/86869

I will add the gerrit link at the commit message of this PR.

Is it correct to assume there is only one associated "controlled_by" object? What is the correct behavior if there is more than one?

You are correct. It’s safer not to assume there’s only one endpoint. 
I will update the logic to handle cases with multiple 'controlled_by' objects or at least add a check for it. Thanks for pointing this out!
Done

Only the first in the subtree is being used, but I'm still wondering what the behavior should be if there is more than one?

Whether to handle multiple control objects as an error, debug info, or just use the first is something I'd like one of the maintainers to set the direction for.

Hi Janet,

Thanks for the heads-up. To my knowledge, there should only be one control object associated with this path in our current architecture. However, I will sync with Ed and Gunnar to confirm the expected behavior for edge cases.

Additionally, since I’ll be working on the PATCH method next, I’d like to get your thoughts on a refactoring idea:

I’m planning to refactor afterGetAssociatedSubTreeForPowerCap by adding a callback function as an input. This would allow us to reuse the same GetAssociatedSubTree logic for both GET and PATCH operations, avoiding code duplication.

Does this approach sound good to you? I'll update the patch once I have feedback from the maintainers.
Yes, code reuse seems like a good idea. Usually when same function is used for PATCH/GET we let the caller handle the error. (I.e. the not found error may be treated differently by GET than PATCH.)
OK, thanks!
Done

Might as well use mapper that gets the objects and their interfaces since it can constrain the search to interfaces implemented.
See: https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/architecture/object-mapper.md#getassociatedsubtree

That's a great suggestion. I will switch to getAssociatedSubTree instead. This will not only allow me to constrain the search to specific interfaces but also help address the previous concern about handling multiple associations more robustly. Thanks!
Done

Why split these routes out? There have been recent changes combining 
multiple requestRoutes* functions into single ones per file. This change
 goes against that direction.
Done

Similar to other file, seems like using GetAssociatedSubtree here would be better.
https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/architecture/object-mapper.md#getassociatedsubtree

Overall this looks good to me. I just have the one outstanding question for Ed or Gunnar on how more than one control object should be handled.

Thanks!

Hi Gunnar and Ender, I'm currently working on rebasing 47300. As part of the rebase I plan to put it on top of this commit and reuse some of the functions created here. So you may wish to hold off on the review of that one until I've updated it.

Thanks for the heads up, Janet!
I'll wait for your update on 47300 before taking another look. 
Let me know if you need any clarification on the functions I implemented.

Hi Ender,
I've pushed a new commit [1] on top of this one. It makes some interface changes to some of the PowerLimitWatts functions added in this commit. The changes are intended to make reuse of these functions for the Chassis commit simpler.

I've tested with the Chassis commit [2] and pushed an update to that commit which uses these functions.

If you could review these commits to make sure the Processor/Chassis PowerLimitWatts commits are heading in the same direction. 

Note: I tested with the Chassis paths but couldn't test the updated functions for the Processor paths.

[1] https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/87955
[2] https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/47300

I reviewed the PDI and noticed that the controlled_by association used in this patch — from the GPU inventory path to the Power.Cap object — is not formally defined in xyz/openbmc_project/Control/Power/Cap.interface.yaml. The spec only defines the
  controlling/controlled_by association with xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.Chassis as the required endpoint interface, not Inventory.Item.Accelerator.

I will address this by either adding Inventory.Item.Accelerator to the PDI

Also, I have tested and reviewed your change 87955. It does not affect the /redfish/v1/Systems/<str>/Processors/GPU_*/EnvironmentMetrics path, and I think the refactoring looks great
Thank you for the review and test of 87955. Would you mind commenting on that commit to indicate the testing you did?
Sure! I'll add a comment on 87955 with my test results.

Removing the parameter entirely is cleaner.
